RULING 4 (charge): confirmed NO change to what any tenant is charged, when or how much - the billing_usage increment and the 'consumed' credit delta are the same calls with the same numbers; the only new write is an INSERT into a new table inside the same tx. One failure-behaviour change to state on the card: a journal INSERT that throws now rolls back the debit with it (5 sites propagate, offer-finalize swallows) - amount unchanged, so gate stays 'architecture', not irreversible. Repo law: tenancy manifest listing is in the write set (good); a new table also needs the *-tenancy.test.ts proof (listed). verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1,3-8 are node:test over .ts modules on the unit DB and would catch a wrong split or a missing row; case 2 (golden byte-identical) is a guard that is green before by design and must be declared as such for flawless_strict.

verdicts.title: Quality board prices each pick and pins the cheapest model within noise
verdicts.premise_notes: All 8 premise bullets hold: QualityCell (llm-quality.ts:24-37) has no cost; bake_quality._cell (:55-88) drops cost_usd and :99 groups by (use_case, model) dropping provider; runner.py records cost_usd (:290-291) and summarize computes costPerTaskUsd (:359); ModelsQualityOverview.tsx:18-20/:142-179 as cited; bestModelForUseCase/matrixSlug are unused; llm-model-matrix.md:103-111 hand table; saveRoutingPin (modelsRoutingActions.ts:24-61) with the MODEL_ROUTING_STALE guard exists; tmp/bench/round-20260811/n4-* records exist locally and an in-memory re-bake reproduces the committed cells with 0 differences. FIGURE ERRORS (immaterial to the design): API row counts are 64/24/32 (120/120 with cost), not 32/12/16 (60/60); medians differ slightly from the card's (gemini 0.0036 vs 0.0038, sonnet 0.1669 vs 0.1807, jd_ingest opus 0.2450 vs 0.2559) - opus is ~68x gemini, so the >=50 case holds. THREE GAPS: (1) the noise band is never defined - acceptance 4/5 hinge on 'inside the band at judges=4' for a 0.1 gap and 'outside' for a 0.7 gap, so a builder can tune the constant to the fixture, which makes the two cases unfalsifiable as written; (2) the committed bake was judged with 'fable-5' but bake_quality's default --judge is 'claude-cli' - a re-bake that omits --judge fable-5 rewrites the file; --measured-at does not exist yet (the card adds it - fine); (3) PUT /api/llm/config also requires requireModelAdmin (:56-57), so the Pin button 403s for non-admin readers - pickRowState has no state for it.
verdicts.floor_notes: M / effort 7 / impact 8 / risk 5 / 13 files + 2 new, ~650-800 lines incl. the regenerated scores file (+~80): at the edge. Gate contract. 4-locale keys and design tokens in scope (design:check). llm-quality-scores.ts is GENERATED - the builder re-bakes, never hand-edits. Existing llm-quality.test.ts:76-82 'opus top on 12 of 15' must stay green (case 3 is a guard). test_llm_bake_quality.py already exists (82 lines) - correctly listed as existing.
verdicts.ambition_why: Pricing the pick and pinning the cheapest statistically-tied model from the board is the decision the operator actually has to make, and the data to make it is already recorded and thrown away; it is a strong UX move on an operator surface.
verdicts.grounding_why: Structure and line citations are exact; the bench figures are approximately right but several are misquoted, and the model-admin gate on the PUT is missed.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cost-median and targets cases are sharp, but the recommendation cases depend on an undefined noise band the builder chooses after seeing the fixture, so they cannot be written to fail for the right reason before the implementation.
verdicts.revise: Define the noise band numerically on the card (e.g. band = 0.15 composite points at judges >= 4, 0.30 below - stated beside QUALITY_WEIGHTS) so acceptance 4 and 5 are fixed before the build, and note that the re-bake must pass --judge fable-5 and that pickRowState needs a 'pin_forbidden' state when the reader is not a model admin.

verdicts.premise_notes: All 8 premise bullets hold and the probe reproduces: WARN_MARKERS (sanity-checks.ts:17-18) tests false on pipeline.py:183 'Blind screening PARTIAL ... Verify manually.' and :146 'Structured job context was unreadable ...', true on :817 'Score section missing - defaulted to 0'; verdict.ts:43-45 treats the defaulted 0 as finite and VerdictBanner.tsx:41 paints it Weak; authenticity.py:205 re-derives the band by substring; models.py:345 list[str] and schemas.generated.ts:56 z.array(z.string()); analyze-run.ts:588 and provenance-dossier.ts:128 consume the regex. schemas.generated.ts is AUTO-GENERATED and committed - the builder edits models.py and runs schemas:gen (typecheck does it anyway); listing it in the write set is correct as a regenerated file. The five exact-string Python tests exist and several assert exact lists (test_salary_sanity.py:32/:39), so the 'string wrappers stay byte-identical' constraint is real and binding. One path the card misses: analyze-run.ts also STORES the defaulted score (0) on the analyses row, so History and calibrationPairs see a 0 that verdict.ts alone will not unpaint - a known-gap line, not a premise failure. seed_analyses.py:495/525 also builds sanity_checks and is outside the write set - safe only because trust_findings is optional (it is).
verdicts.floor_notes: L / effort 7 / impact 8 / risk 6 / 14 files + 2 new, ~550-800 lines: at the edge but inside. Gate contract (the wire field is additive and nullish). Collisions inside this deck: analyze-run.ts with billing-subscriptions/A (different hunks: :588 vs :563) and ResultPanel.tsx + docs/features/candidates/README.md with results-core/B - build A before B (B's brief reads severity if A lands). docs/features/candidates/README.md is also r06 candidate-apply-flow/A's (append). Case 4 (byte-identical sanity_checks) is a guard - declare it.
verdicts.ambition_why: Categorising the finding at birth and retiring the last prose-regex classifier in the product, across two runtimes, is exactly the principal's move; it also unlocks localisation and decision gating on findings.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every line is exact and the regex misfire is reproduced by a probe rather than argued.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Python finding cases and TS ledger/legacy-fallback/verdict cases are sharp and pre-writable; case 4 is a guard and the .tsx consumers are covered only by the .ts module behind them.

verdicts.title: Decide with the flags in view: Advance acknowledges them, the record keeps them
verdicts.premise_notes: All 7 premise bullets hold: DispositionEditor is mounted with slug/initialDisposition/initialNote only (ResultPanel.tsx:261-265); pick() (:62-77) saves optimistically with no precondition; QualityStrip renders below the decision row (:282 vs :257-280); credentials.py:120-123 asks to 'verify before advancing'; route.ts:96-111 stores disposition+note and echoes to events; analyses.ts:280 UPDATE and :294-300 calibrationPairs; pipeline.ts:1665 detail composition. REFUSAL_ERRORS exists (api-response.ts:525) and i18n-check requires errors.<CODE> in all four catalogs - catalogs are in the write set. GAP the card does not handle: the editor is OPTIMISTIC - pick() sets 'advance' locally before the server answers (:64), and there is an 800 ms note autosave (:82-86) and a keepalive unmount flush (:95-116) that both re-PATCH {disposition, note}; after a 409 DISPOSITION_ACK_REQUIRED the local state still says 'advance', so every later autosave and the flush re-send an un-acknowledged advance and 409 again, and save() treats any non-OK as the generic saveFailed. The only disposition PATCH callers are the editor's two sites (useAnalyzeForm.ts:489 sends githubAnalysis only, earlier branch), and analyses-routes.test.ts seeds payloads with no sanityChecks, so no other caller breaks. ResultPanel.contract.test.ts:29/39 regex-checks '<DispositionEditor\s+slug={analysisSlug}' - the new analysis prop must follow slug. The route test the Method names is not in the write set.
verdicts.floor_notes: M / effort 6 / impact 8 / risk 5 / 12 files + 2 new, ~400-550 lines: inside. Gate policy-tighten (a recruiter must acknowledge each open flag to advance and give a reason to pass a strong read) - allowed; it tightens the human decision, loosens nothing. Repo law: new code + 4 catalog entries (in scope); nullable column additive; analyses is already in the tenancy manifest. COLLISION: app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts is in r06 db-pipeline-store A AND B (both building now) and r06 candidate-apply-flow/A - build after all three land; the hunk here is small (recordAnalysisDispositionEvents detail). Inside the deck: ResultPanel.tsx + candidates README with results-core/A - build after A.
verdicts.ambition_why: Binding the decision to the machine verdict it overrode - at the click and at the door, and in the record the calibration set later trusts - is the fairness-and-defensibility move the product promises in AiDisclosure and does not keep.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every premise line is exact, and the card correctly limits the gate to transitions to advance so legacy decisions and note-only edits are never locked.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: The pure brief/gate matrix and the route 409/200 cases are pre-writable and sharp; the editor's optimistic-state behaviour after a 409 has no case, so a build that loops 409s on autosave would pass every listed case.
verdicts.revise: Add an acceptance case for the editor's three PATCH paths: on a 409 DISPOSITION_ACK_REQUIRED the optimistic disposition rolls back to the stored value, and the note autosave (:82-86) and keepalive unmount flush (:95-116) carry `acknowledged` (or send note-only) so they never re-issue an un-acknowledged advance; and add the route test file (app/api/analyses/[slug]/route.test.ts or the existing analyses-routes.test.ts) to the write_set.

verdicts.title: Steps declare the authority they write: the run derives from intent x seat
verdicts.premise_notes: All 10 premise bullets hold: the '/' gate is per user (onboarding-gate.ts:26-29) and a redeemed invite lands on '/' (invite-result.ts:100-101); hiringOnly is the only predicate (setupSteps.ts:55-62); roles.ts CAPS: owner has org:manage, admin members:manage/team:manage/pipeline:write/read, recruiter and hiring_manager pipeline:write/read, viewer read; org-actions refuse without org:manage (:55/:71/:103); language is written on every run (setupOnboardingFinish.ts:34/:58); Company requires orgName (:118) seeded only from the cookie (SetupCompanyStep.tsx:64-71); invites POST requires members:manage (:32); PUT /api/brand is requireOperator only (:51-53) and requireOperator admits any valid non-demo session; the tour tile fires sim.start() for every seat (:137-139) vs TOUR_CAPABILITY pipeline:write; the wizard imports no capability resolver; GET /api/me/onboarding is ungated and already serves {scope}. setupSteps.test.ts:35-40 pins the six ids with a seat-less HIRE, so INITIAL_SETUP.seat=null failing open is load-bearing.
verdicts.floor_notes: M / effort 6 / impact 8 / risk 5 / 13 files + 3 new, ~350-450 lines: inside. Gate architecture. RULING 5: the owner's wizard is unchanged by construction - callerOrgCapabilities()/callerCapabilities() both return OWNER_CAPS in open mode (current-user.ts:162-163, :46-52) and for a password-operator session, null seat fails open, and e2e/journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts:152-262 walks all six steps in open mode, so it keeps passing. It IS a tighten of the wizard path (nothing is granted, steps and parts are only removed for seats that cannot land them). BUT the premise names a server hole (an invitee re-skins the org via PUT /api/brand) that the card does not close: app/api/brand/route.ts is NOT in the write set and the Flow only hides the Company step client-side, so 'two live mis-writes close' is true only inside the wizard - any member can still PUT /api/brand directly or from Settings > Branding, and the tour-tile fix is likewise client-only. Design note: the seat arrives after mount, so a non-owner first sees six steps and then a shorter list while stepIndex is restored from the draft (useSetupDraft.ts:62-72) - the builder must not persist seat into the draft and must clamp the index. Collides with shell-setup-wizard/B on setupOnboardingFinish.ts (both touch the :58 language line), OnboardingExperience.tsx, setupSteps.ts, SetupHandoffSummary.tsx, its test, catalogs and app-structure.md - build A before B, never one wave. useSetupDraft.ts is a hook (not unit-testable); OnboardingExperience/SetupHandoffSummary are .tsx; cases 1-7 are .ts-testable, case 8 has a route-test precedent (me/capabilities/route.test.ts).
verdicts.ambition_why: Deriving the run from intent x seat, with steps declaring the capability their answers need, is the correct model for a wizard whose second-largest audience is invitees; it stops short of the server-side finish door the runner-up names.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every line is exact and the owner-fold reasoning is verified, but the card claims to close a server hole (brand PUT) that its write set never touches.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: relevantSteps/finishPartsFor/handoffExits/parseSetupSeat cases for owner, null, recruiter, admin and viewer are sharp and pre-writable; the late-arriving-seat index shift has no case.
verdicts.revise: Either add app/api/brand/route.ts (+ its test) to the write_set and gate PUT on requireOrgCapability('org:manage') with a coded 403 (roles.ts:25 already declares org profile/settings owner-only, so the owner path is untouched), or strike 'two live mis-writes close' from Expected impact and state that the brand PUT hole stays open and is filed as a follow-up - the card must do one of the two, not claim the first while doing neither.

verdicts.title: Finish ends on a receipt: share each invite link, retry only what failed
verdicts.premise_notes: All 7 premise bullets hold: POST /api/org/invites returns {invite} including token (route.ts:64 via inviteMember -> createInvite), createInvite only INSERTs (invites.ts:50-72); setupOnboardingFinish.ts:158 discards the body; SetupInviteResult has no token (:77); readyMeta moved to en.json:9582 and inviteCreated to :7364 (same text); copyInviteUrl (workspaceAdminHelpers.ts:14-16); the finally block (OnboardingExperience.tsx:240-249) clears the draft, stamps completed and closes whatever the fold; the refused fold carries code + addresses (:46-48); SetupLeaveConfirm occupies the same card slot (SetupOnboardingWizard.tsx:81-82). The existing test stub {invite:{}} keeps passing if token falls back to null. GAPS: persistOnboardingSetup returns only the fold, so exposing raw results is a signature change; the invites route's 409 `{error: result.reason}` carries NO code, so isRetryable would classify a permanent no_workspace refusal as retryable (null code); the language write at :58 is unconditional and finishRemainder must gate it - the same line card A edits.
verdicts.floor_notes: Declared M, but the honest estimate is ~500-650 lines across 13 files + 1 new, FOUR of them .tsx (OnboardingExperience +~50 on a 300-line file, SetupOnboardingWizard, SetupHandoffSummary, the new SetupFinishReceipt ~130) - this is an L by lines and by untestable surface. Gate none. Acceptance 6's second half (stamp + clearDraft on the receipt's Done, deferred sim.start) lives only in .tsx and cannot be a node:test case; case 7 is key parity, not wording. Collides with shell-setup-wizard/A on 7 files incl. the :58 language line and the tour tile - build strictly after A. Catalogs shared with 7 r06 cards (lock).
verdicts.ambition_why: A receipt with the invite links and a targeted retry is a real experience gap closed (kp sends no invite mail, so today the links vanish), but it is a commit-boundary polish of one flow rather than a structural move.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every claim, including the discarded token and the finally block, is exact; the two moved catalog lines are trivial.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: finishReceipt/isRetryable/finishRemainder/finishNext are pure and pre-writable, but the change that matters most - the stamp and draft clear moving out of finally - is .tsx-only and has no case a wrong build would fail; isRetryable's rule is also under-specified for a code-less 409.
verdicts.revise: Re-size the card to L, split acceptance 6 into the pure finishNext case (kept) and a source-shape pin that OnboardingExperience.tsx's finish() no longer calls clearDraft/stamp in `finally`, and make isRetryable treat a code-less non-2xx from /api/org/invites as PERMANENT unless the status is 429/5xx (the route's 409 carries no code); sequence after shell-setup-wizard/A.

verdicts.title: The director's ledger is the transcript of record, not the hang-up POST
verdicts.premise_notes: All 7 premise bullets hold: complete/route.ts:126-131 builds the transcript from body.transcript, :252 persists it, :408 scores it, and the route never reads interview_events; director-step.ts:152-159 persists every finalized turn idempotently (interview-events.ts:117 ON CONFLICT ... WHERE kind='turn' DO NOTHING) with ackSeq backpressure (:33-35); resume.ts:22/:38 hand back only the last 40 prior turns and VoiceInterview.tsx:999 seeds turnsRef from them; director.ts:706/:726 verify quotes against the LEDGER's candidate turns; discarded-turns.ts:43-54 is a prefix rule; the spoken eval harness (session_runner.py:206, app_client.py:191-206) never posts /director. RULING 7: ADR 0010 (keep the provider brain, add our director; provenance checked not trusted; a reconnect resumes from the record) - this card CONFORMS and extends rule 4 to the scorecard's input; internal ids stay off the wire as long as ledger rows are mapped to {role,text,at} and seq/attempt are dropped (publicSessionView already exposes only session.id + transcript). /api/interview/complete is a public token route (public-routes.ts:114). GAP: the duplicate check exists TWICE - :138-159 (session already completed: discardedTurnCount(session.transcript, submitted) on the RAW unclamped body, then 409) runs BEFORE the consent check (:166) and the rate limit (:173); :258-264 (lost race) compares the clamped array. The card's Flow step 3 reads the ledger 'after the consent + rate-limit refusals' and feeds the merged array to the duplicate check - both cannot hold; acceptance 7 (honest beacon on a 67-turn record must not 409) forces the ledger read inside the completed-session branch, i.e. a scoped DB read before the throttle on a public door. Also: once a session hits MAX_INTERVIEW_EVENTS_PER_SESSION the ledger stops (director-step.ts:151) - the anchor-and-tail rule handles it (the body still carries the ledger's last turn and everything after), which the card should say.
verdicts.floor_notes: M / effort 6 / impact 8 / risk 6 / 5 files (3 new), ~550-650 lines: inside. Gate contract. Repo law: the projection allowlist rule holds; listInterviewEvents(sessionId, workspaceId, opts) is workspace-scoped in SQL with a JS-side kinds filter (default limit 5000). Five existing complete-*.test.ts suites use app/_lib/testing/unit-db.ts and complete-reconnect-billing already seeds appendInterviewEvents - the template exists. COLLISION: app/api/interview/complete/route.ts is also in billing-subscriptions/A's write set (:355 recordMeterUsage source argument) - build voice A first, billing A after, or merge the one-line hunk.
verdicts.ambition_why: Making the server's own append-only record the thing that is persisted and scored - closing both the resumed-call amnesia and a candidate-side tamper path into the Interview->Offer gate - is precisely what a principal fixes once the director exists.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every line is exact, the passthrough rule for undirected sessions is derived from the eval harness's real behaviour, and the ADR relationship is correctly read.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: The eight cases (passthrough, resumed opening restored, rewrite refused, insertion counted, tail kept, anchor miss degrades, honest beacon still 200, one array feeds both writes) each fail against today's route and pin a distinct rule of the merge.
verdicts.revise: Fix Flow step 3: read the session's ledger turns once, right after the session is loaded and before the completed-session duplicate check at :138-159 (not after the consent/rate-limit refusals), and route BOTH duplicate checks (:146 and :258) through the merged array, so acceptance 7 is satisfiable; add one line that a ledger truncated at MAX_INTERVIEW_EVENTS_PER_SESSION still anchors on its last stored turn.

verdicts.title: Compare grid reads the director: covered, asked, or never reached per axis
verdicts.premise_notes: All 5 premise bullets hold: interview-scorecard.ts:62-67 puts 'not assessed' ON the scale as a 3; director-types.ts:56-59 blocks carry competency server-side and :265-267/:285 are persisted events; deriveDirectorState (director.ts:182, exported, pure) yields coveredBlockIds/begunBlockIds (:139-141) and topic_covered is accepted only with a verified quote (:698-711); compare/route.ts:47-51 attaches nothing from events or agenda; interviews.ts:67 interviewedForJob has no mode filter while :319 does; rehearse/route.ts:146-154 mints mode 'test' with jobId set, so rehearsals really do enter the cohort. README:1709-1724 documents the sentinel. RULING 7: conforms to ADR 0010 (reads the director's record, adds no client-trusted signal); this is an OPERATOR surface (compare is behind the proxy session gate, not a public token route - it has no requireOperator call of its own, relying on currentWorkspace()), so 'no quote/question text' is a self-imposed data-minimisation rule, not the candidate-wire rule - harmless. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) 'id + agenda now ride interviewedForJob's existing SELECT' is wrong - the SELECT (:62-68) reads s.id but not agenda_json (stored by setInterviewAgenda :765-768, parsed at :242) and does not return id (:98-110); both must be added; deriveDirectorState needs {agenda, events, currentAttempt, attemptStartedAtMs, nowMs}, so a completed session must supply an attempt count and a clock; (2) must_ask_unasked is written ONLY on the end_interview tool call (director.ts:794-798), so a call that dropped without ending has none - mustAsksUnasked === 0 is ambiguous between 'all asked' and 'never recorded', and acceptance 5's count-only chip would read the second as the first.
verdicts.floor_notes: M / effort 6 / impact 8 / risk 5. write_set has 15 entries INCLUDING the 4 new files (at the ~15 floor, not over); ~650-800 lines - at the edge, the three test files are the bulk. Gate none; 4-locale keys and design tokens in scope. Only JobsCompareInterviewsCohortTable.tsx is .tsx. No r06 code collision (catalogs only); docs/features/interviews/README.md shared with voice-interview-api/A (append). The mode='candidate' clause on interviewedForJob is a behaviour change for the compare cohort and the CSV - correct and pinned by case 7.
verdicts.ambition_why: Putting the director's coverage record on the cell where a hire is weighed - distinguishing 'asked and weak' from 'never asked' and flagging where the model's rating disagrees with the record - is the unassessed-competency standard applied where it matters; the rehearsal fix rides along.
verdicts.grounding_why: The defect and the data are cited exactly, but the SELECT does not carry what the card says it carries and the must-ask event's write condition makes 0 ambiguous.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Pure axis-coverage cases, the cross-attempt derivation, the null-for-undirected case, the disagreement flags, the CSV blanking and the mode filter each fail today; case 5 as written cannot tell a dropped call from a clean one.
verdicts.revise: Make coverage.mustAsksUnasked `number | null` - null when the session has no end_interview event (must_ask_unasked is only written there, director.ts:794-798) - and amend acceptance 5 to assert the null case renders no chip; and correct the Flow to add agenda_json + session id to interviewedForJob's SELECT and return shape (they are not on it today).
